headline: Congress vows to battle delimitation bill in special session
hook: Parliament meets on Nov 30, but not for women’s quota.
what: The government has scheduled a special parliamentary sitting starting November 30 to discuss the delimitation bill. Congress says the meeting is about redrawing constituencies, not the women’s reservation proposal, and it will oppose the bill strongly.
why: The outcome could reshape electoral boundaries, affecting future elections. Young voters should watch the debate as it may influence political representation.

headline: KPCC chief seeks talk with Gandhi, Kharge amid Kerala party split
hook: Congress’s Kerala head wants a sit‑down as factions clash.
what: KPCC chief Sunny Joseph said he wants to meet Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge. He made the request as internal disagreements surface in the state Congress. He declined to comment on the ongoing war of words and the flex boards supporting different leaders.
why: The meeting could shape the party’s stance in Kerala, affecting future elections and youth representation. Keep an eye on any shifts in strategy.

headline: Chirakkara Panchayat Launches Tourism Plan for Polachira Wetlands
hook: Your next weekend getaway could be a newly promoted wetland spot!
what: The local governing body of Chirakkara in Kollam announced a new tourism development project focused on the Polachira wetlands. The plan aims to improve visitor facilities and promote eco‑tourism.
why: Young travelers can look forward to better amenities and nature experiences nearby. Keep an eye out for upcoming events or tours in the area.

headline: SC declines urgent listing in Ramayana film case
hook: A new Ramayana adaptation sparked debate, and the Supreme Court made a comment.
what: The Supreme Court did not hear an urgent plea about the Ramayana: Rise of a Legend film. The plea involved claims about facts in the film. The court also said that someone with a different view could make a film.
why: It matters to young Indian viewers because it touches on storytelling and how sacred stories are shown. They can watch or talk about the film while the court matter continues.

headline: Two Italians die in Kuwait drone strike, Iran denies involvement
hook: A deadly drone hit Kuwait, sparking a diplomatic flare‑up.
what: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian nationals. Italy and Kuwait confirmed the fatalities and blamed Iran. Tehran has rejected the accusation.
why: Rising tensions could affect regional stability and travel safety. Stay updated with advisories and news.

headline: Delhi to let public tour Kejriwal’s former ‘Sheesh Mahal’
hook: Your next weekend outing could be inside a former chief minister’s house.
what: The Delhi administration announced that the former residence of Arvind Kejriwal, called ‘Sheesh Mahal’, will be opened for media first, then for visitors. Access will be managed through a ticket system, with tickets expected to cost around ₹20.
why: It offers a chance to see a political landmark at a low price, so students can plan a quick visit if interested.

headline: Sony headphones hit record lows this Black Friday
hook: Grab top‑tier sound without breaking your budget.
what: Sony is offering deep discounts on several wireless headphones for Black Friday, including models priced under $50 and the WH‑1000XM6 at a historic low. The WH‑1000XM4C also dropped to $198, while the WH‑1000XM5 in Midnight Blue is $230 off.
why: For Indian Gen Z, this is a rare chance to own premium audio gear at student‑friendly prices. Check the deals now and compare features before buying.

headline: Gukesh and Sindarov End Game 3 With Draw
hook: Two chess stars could not score the win in Game 3.
what: Game 3 of the FIDE World Chess Championship in Geneva did not produce a winner. Gukesh and Sindarov both tried to win. After three games, no difference was reported between them.
why: For young Indian chess fans, the match is being followed closely. They may want to keep watching the next game.

headline: Supreme Court says legal expert needed for ED attachment orders
hook: Big court rules you can't leave major money freezes to non‑lawyers.
what: The Supreme Court ruled that decisions on Enforcement Directorate attachment cases must involve a judicial member. It said such important decisions cannot be made by a member lacking a legal background.
why: This ensures legal expertise in cases that can affect businesses and individuals, protecting rights. Stay aware of legal processes that could impact your finances.

headline: Parliament to meet from Nov 30 for major delimitation
hook: A fresh electoral map could reshape future elections.
what: The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30. The government plans a large‑scale delimitation exercise to redraw constituency boundaries.
why: New constituency lines can affect representation and voting power, influencing policies that impact youth. Stay informed before the next elections.

headline: Heavy rain floods Thiruvananthapuram, traffic snarls citywide
hook: Rainwater turned streets into rivers, commuters stuck.
what: Intense downpours drenched parts of Thiruvananthapuram, leading to deep water accumulation. Several roads became impassable, causing major traffic jams. Officials faced criticism for lack of readiness.
why: Young commuters may need to plan alternate routes or use public transport. It highlights the need for better city drainage.

headline: X Adds Parental Controls for Teens After 20 Years
hook: Parents can now oversee what teens see on X.
what: The social media platform X, linked to Elon Musk, brought in parental controls for teenagers. Such controls are meant to let parents and guardians oversee what minors see. The update came after a 20-year gap.
why: This could affect how young people use social media. Parents and guardians now have a way to guide what children view on X.

headline: Karnataka CM challenges ASHA workers' demand for state guarantee
hook: The chief minister says asking the state for a letter is unfair.
what: Karnataka Chief Minister Shivakumar responded to protesting ASHA workers. He asked why they wanted a written assurance from the state when their appointments came from the central government. He added that no government can be blackmailed.
why: The dispute highlights how health‑worker job security can become a political issue. Young people should keep track of such policy debates that affect public health services.

headline: Missed SIP payment won’t hurt CIBIL but may cost fees
hook: Skip a SIP? Your credit stays safe, but your bank might charge.
what: If a SIP debit fails, the mutual fund units stay unchanged and the CIBIL score is not affected. Banks can levy a return charge for the failed transaction, and repeated failures may lead to SIP cancellation.
why: Young investors should keep an eye on their bank balance to avoid fees and ensure regular SIP payments so their investment plan stays on track.

headline: Cabinet backs ₹11,000 crore plan for home-made construction gear
hook: Big boost for Indian factories making building machines.
what: The Union Cabinet gave the green light to a scheme worth ₹11,000 crore aimed at strengthening the domestic production of construction and infrastructure equipment. The program, called the CIE Manufacturing Ecosystem, will provide incentives to manufacturers across the country.
why: It could create jobs and lower costs for building projects, which matters for young people looking for work or affordable housing. Companies may start hiring locally as they expand.

headline: Kerala Leader Claims Phone Tapping
hook: A top Kerala leader says his phone is being tapped
what: A Kerala leader has claimed that his phone is being tapped and he is under constant surveillance. He admits to giving wrong information to mislead those listening. This is allegedly done to counter the surveillance.
why: This matter raises concerns about privacy and surveillance in the state. Young Indians should be aware of their rights and the laws surrounding phone tapping.

headline: Central DA rises to 63%, states follow suit
hook: Your take‑home could jump after the latest allowance hike.
what: The government lifted Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief by three points, setting the combined rate at 63%. Several state governments have announced comparable increases. The 8th Pay Commission is expected to hand in its final report by May 2027.
why: Higher DA means more immediate cash for government staff, while the pending commission report will shape future salary structures and pensions. Employees should stay updated for upcoming changes.

headline: SBI opens 1,540 Junior Associate positions
hook: Bank jobs alert for fresh grads!
what: State Bank of India announced hiring for 1,540 junior associate roles. The vacancy details were shared publicly.
why: Bank jobs are a popular entry point for many youngsters. Keep an eye on the official SBI portal for application steps.

headline: Vance denies pardon amid rising China chip scrutiny, Huang live
hook: A live chat with Nvidia’s boss meets a firm stance on pardons.
what: During a live session, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appeared as Vance said there will be no pardon. The discussion comes as scrutiny over Chinese chip activities intensifies.
why: For Indian tech‑savvy youth, it signals ongoing geopolitical tension that could affect chip availability and AI projects. Stay informed on policy shifts that may impact tech careers.

headline: Tripura’s First Woman ATC Bipasha Hrangkhawl in KBC
hook: The woman who handles plane traffic from Tripura is now on KBC.
what: Bipasha Hrangkhawl is Tripura’s first woman air traffic controller. She took part in KBC Season 18.
why: It matters because a woman from Tripura took part in a national TV quiz show. It can be a talking point for young viewers.

headline: SP pledges ₹40k yearly cash aid for UP’s BPL women, seniors
hook: A new cash boost could hit millions of Uttar Pradesh families.
what: The Samajwadi Party announced a scheme to give ₹40,000 per year to women, elderly and needy members of Below‑Poverty‑Line households in Uttar Pradesh. The payment is planned as an annual transfer under the party’s 2027 election agenda.
why: If implemented, the benefit could support low‑income households and influence young voters concerned about financial security. Keep an eye on the policy details as the election approaches.

headline: Ellyse Perry’s 84 leads Sixers to six‑wicket victory
hook: A stellar knock turned the chase into a breeze for Sydney.
what: In the 35th match of the 2026 Women’s Big Bash League, Ellyse Perry stayed unbeaten on 84 runs. Sydney Sixers chased down Melbourne Stars’ 161‑run target, winning by six wickets after early setbacks.
why: The result shows how a big innings can decide a T20 game, encouraging young fans to watch the league and try cricket themselves.

headline: Tamil Nadu gives govt dads 15 days paternity leave
hook: Dad duties just got official time off in TN
what: The Tamil Nadu government approved a 15‑day paternity leave for its male staff. Female staff already receive a year of maternity leave.
why: It helps new fathers balance work and family, setting a precedent for other states. Young workers can check their eligibility and plan accordingly.

headline: Three BJP-RSS members sentenced to life for Kerala leader killing
hook: A court orders life terms in a high‑profile political murder.
what: A court in Kerala handed life imprisonment to three individuals linked to the BJP and RSS for the murder of a Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader. The verdict concludes the trial over the killing.
why: The ruling highlights the legal response to political violence, reminding young citizens that such acts carry serious consequences. Stay aware of local news and the rule of law.

headline: Heavy rain drenches Thiruvananthapuram, East Fort records 91 mm
hook: Rain hammered the capital, prompting alerts across nine districts.
what: Thiruvananthapuram experienced intense rainfall, with East Fort receiving 91 mm in just one hour. Meteorological officials issued a yellow alert covering nine districts in the state.
why: The sudden downpour can cause waterlogging and disrupt travel, so students should stay updated on local advisories.

headline: Muslim translator renders Hindu leader’s Bible-inspired talks into English
hook: A cross‑faith collaboration bridges Kerala’s political and religious worlds
what: Muslim translator Rauf Rumi has translated the Bible‑inspired speeches of Kerala politician V D Satheesan into English. The translation makes the leader’s messages accessible to a wider audience.
why: It highlights interfaith cooperation and shows young Indians that collaboration across religions is possible. Readers can appreciate the shared cultural fabric of Kerala.

headline: Gold ETFs split: only two beat a year of falling prices
hook: Find out why most gold funds are losing money while a couple thrive.
what: Gold prices have slipped recently. Out of all gold exchange‑traded funds, just two posted gains over the past year. Experts say the performance gap stems from differences in fund metrics.
why: Young investors need to look beyond headline returns and check key factors before picking a gold ETF. Understanding the five metrics can help avoid losses.

headline: Sensex jumps 390 points, IT and realty lead gains
hook: Foreign money fuels a fresh rally in Indian markets.
what: The benchmark Sensex closed 390 points higher, while the Nifty settled at 25,885. Shares in the IT and realty sectors posted strong gains, driving the rise.
why: Young investors should note the impact of overseas fund flows on market moves and consider tech stocks that are attracting attention.

headline: Yellow rain alerts issued for 10 Kerala districts
hook: Heavy showers may hit your area—check if schools close
what: The India Meteorological Department has issued yellow alerts for ten districts in Kerala for November 26 and 27, indicating isolated heavy rain. The warnings are district‑wise and include possible disruptions to school and college schedules.
why: Students should verify if their school or college is closed and plan travel accordingly.

headline: Apple launches its 7th Indian store in Hyderabad
hook: New Apple outlet opens Dec 10 – check it out!
what: Apple is set to open its seventh retail outlet in India, located in Hyderabad. The store will open on December 10. A decorative barricade at the Kukatpally site shows a pearl‑inspired Apple logo with iridescent colours.
why: The launch expands Apple’s presence for fans who want hands‑on experience with devices. Teens can visit to explore the latest iPhone models and accessories.

headline: Nvidia pauses server shipments to four SE Asian nations
hook: New US rules force Nvidia to stop deliveries in the region.
what: Nvidia has stopped sending its AI servers to four countries in Southeast Asia. The halt comes after fresh US export restrictions were implemented last week.
why: The restriction could delay access to AI hardware for students and startups in those markets, so they may need to explore alternative suppliers.

headline: Tamil Nadu grants 15‑day paternity leave for married govt staff
hook: Dad‑to‑be can now take two weeks off around the birth.
what: The state will allow married male government employees to take 15 days off either before their child is born or within six months after. The leave applies to all such staff.
why: It helps new fathers balance work and family early on, encouraging involvement in childcare.

headline: India urges Netflix to pull Pakistani series
hook: The government says the show must stay off Indian screens.
what: The Indian government has asked Netflix to stop streaming the Pakistani drama 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' in the country. Officials say the platform should respect its earlier promise not to host Pakistani content.
why: Young viewers rely on streaming services for entertainment, so this could affect what’s available on Netflix India. Users should check the app for any changes to the catalogue.

headline: India tells Netflix to block Pakistani shows
hook: Streaming platform faces government order over a popular series.
what: The Indian ministry has asked Netflix to follow an advisory issued on May 8, 2025, and remove Pakistani content. The request comes amid controversy surrounding the series “Jo Bachay…”.
why: Young viewers may see fewer shows from Pakistan on Netflix, so check the platform for updated content lists.

headline: Elon Musk promises two SpaceX shares to every US child
hook: A billionaire’s gift could turn kids into future shareholders.
what: Elon Musk announced he will allocate two SpaceX shares to each child in the United States. The pledge aims to give every American youngster a stake in the company.
why: Such a move could spark interest in space technology and investing among youth. Indian teens can watch how high‑profile founders distribute equity.

headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang shares therapy update, apologizes at town hall
hook: Even tech giants need mental health breaks.
what: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang told employees he is attending therapy and apologized during a company-wide town hall. The comments came after recent pressure on the AI chip maker.
why: It shows that even top CEOs face mental‑health challenges, encouraging openness about therapy. Young professionals can see it as a cue to prioritize wellbeing.

headline: Vivo Watch GT 2 Comes to India with Curved Screen
hook: The Vivo Watch GT 2 has a curved screen and long battery life.
what: Vivo has brought its Watch GT 2 into India. The wearable features a curved AMOLED screen and can run for up to 25 days after one charge. It is available in two colour choices.
why: For young Indian tech fans, this is a fresh wrist wearable to watch. The known details focus on the screen and battery.

headline: Mumbai Police issue LOC against CJP leader Saurav Das
hook: A legal notice may restrict the activist’s movements.
what: Mumbai police have issued a Look Out Circular against CJP leader Saurav Das. The central government informed the Delhi High Court about the action. Das’s counsel says he was not told about the LOC or its purpose.
why: Such notices can limit a person’s ability to travel, showing how legal steps affect activists. Young people should stay informed about civic and legal developments.

headline: Kerala govt sets up panel to shape new liquor policy
hook: New rules could change drink prices and availability for teens
what: The UDF government in Kerala has created a sub‑committee to draft a liquor policy. The panel will try to balance the state's revenue needs with social, religious, political and health concerns linked to alcohol consumption.
why: Any policy shift may affect the cost and access to alcohol, so young people should keep an eye on upcoming changes.

headline: Supreme Court mandates separate high‑fat, sugar, salt warnings
hook: Packaged snacks will now show clear health alerts.
what: The Supreme Court told the Centre and FSSAI to require distinct warning labels for foods high in fat, sugar or salt. Manufacturers must display each warning separately on packaging.
why: Young consumers can spot unhealthy ingredients quickly and make better snack choices.
